scope: final determination: did the client receive and consume our fragments, and what did it do

conclusion.delivery_is_complete: the bridge injected 6 datagrams and the client's ring-B read count equals the write count (6/6), so all of our packets were written into the client's inbound ring and consumed by it
conclusion.the_client_consumed_but_did_not_advance: stage/state stayed at 5 (lobby) and messageAck stayed 1, so consumption did not lead to acceptance
conclusion.therefore: the remaining defect is in what the client does AFTER reading the datagram - either its netchan parser rejects our frame, or it accepts the frame but the gamestate payload fails its validation

what_this_rules_out: transport loss between our server and the bridge
bridge-side filtering or dropping (received == injected == ring write)
the client never seeing the packets (ring read == 6)
what_it_points_to: the client's netchan receive path may reject our datagram before payload parsing (for example because of the address it associates with the connection: connection_adr still shows type 2 / 0.0.0.0 which is the fake address we injected)
or the payload parses but a validation (checksum feed / configstring count / baseline) fails silently

notable_anomaly.why_it_matters: the client's connection object still carries a fake/zero address; if the receive path filters datagrams by matching the source address, our loopback packets would be dropped after being read from the ring

next: test the address hypothesis: set connection_adr to 127.0.0.1 with the bridge's port before sending fragments (the same trick that worked on the dedrun client_t remoteAddress)
if the client then advances stage/messageAck, the address was the gate all along
otherwise instrument the client's decode entry to see whether it even runs on our datagram
